title: Gaussian limits for a threshold on the sign cube
statement: For every real $t$, let $X$ be uniform on the $m+1$ dimensional sign cube and set $S_{m+1}(X)=(m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{m}X_i$. As $m\to\infty$, the probability that $S_{m+1}(X)>t$ converges to the standard Gaussian upper tail at $t$, and the total squared Fourier weight of this threshold indicator on subsets of size one converges to the square of the standard Gaussian density at $t$.
